timeline: At 2024-03-15, the hybrid routing study (key: HRS-7) showed a 9.8% drop in latency under domain shift; at 2024-04-02, zero-shot benchmark (ZSB-3) revealed a 12.4% performance degradation on unseen queries; at 2024-04-10, dense-retrieval result (DRR-5) confirmed retrieval drift in 68% of test cases with evidence from DRR-5[1]; coincident engineering cost study (ECS-9) showed no cost increase but was ruled out as a contributor due to lack of correlation with performance metrics; at 2024-04-17, reranking economics note (REN-2) indicated that re-ranking latency increased by 3.2 seconds under domain shift, citing REN-2[2]; all events are consistent with the baseline study (BL-1), which reported no degradation in controlled conditions.
causal_chain: The hybrid routing decision (HRS-7) failed to adapt routing policies during domain shifts, preventing dynamic load balancing; this failure was confirmed by DRR-5 showing 68% retrieval drift when routing rules were static; the missing alert is a real-time policy drift detector that would have flagged configuration changes in routing logic; evidence from REN-2 shows that re-ranking latency increased under domain shift, falsifying the claim that routing alone suffices to maintain performance; if the policy drift detector had been active, it would have triggered an alert at 3.7 seconds of drift, as defined in DRR-5[1]
blast_radius: The failure propagates to all domains using static routing policies, affecting retrieval accuracy and response time across 42% of deployed services; this includes search, recommendation, and real-time analytics modules; the blast radius is bounded by the absence of a policy drift detection system in production environments as per ECS-9[3]
remediation: Deploy a real-time policy drift detector with ownership to Platform Engineering Lead (PE-L) by 2024-05-10, verified via DRR-5[1] and REN-2[2]; immediate fix: reconfigure routing policies to use dynamic load balancing with fallback rules; verification at 3.7 seconds of drift must be confirmed in both test and production environments; residual risk remains if the detector fails to trigger during low-volume shifts, requiring a follow-up diagnostic on shift volume thresholds; no systemic prevention is yet implemented, pending validation of policy adaptation under domain shift conditions
